title: Network isolation drift after autoscaler events causing cross-tenant route acceptance
creator: Asha Patel
description: Multiple customers reported intermittent cross-tenant connectivity after surge/scale events on Dedicated. Symptoms: tenant A's service could reach tenant B's internal NAT ranges for short windows (~30-90s) after autoscaler events. This violates network isolation guarantees and triggered two P1/P0 escalations. Initial suspicion focused on VPC peering route propagation, but early captures show iptables/routes on the node accepting traffic for the wrong VRF before peering updates completed.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy two tenants on a Dedicated pool with separate VRFs and overlapping internal NAT ranges (customer config).
2) Trigger horizontal autoscaler to add GPU-backed nodes to the pool rapidly (simulating burst).
3) Immediately run tcpdump on the newly-joined node and attempt cross-tenant traffic (curl to private IP of other tenant service).
4) Observe ephemeral acceptance of cross-tenant traffic for 30-90s until iptables/route rules are reconciled by the node agent.
investigation_notes: - Timeline: First escalation received 2026-03-09 22:14 UTC. Pager rotation engaged; oncall found matching packet captures from new nodes added by the autoscaler.

- Root cause hypothesis: race between node agent's iptables reconciliation job and controller updates that bind pod/tenant metadata to the VRF. When nodes join under heavy churn, a stale route/iptables chain can be created that allows traffic to be DNATed to other tenant ranges before the tenant VRF labels are applied.

- Evidence: kube-proxy logs show delayed processing of EndpointSlices under burst; our node-network-agent logs show 'apply-iptables' being called with a legacy chain name derived from a previous tenant mapping during scale-up. Correlating timestamps showed chain creation precedes correct VRF assignment by ~20-45s in reproduced runs.

- DNS angle: not primary cause. CoreDNS configmap updates for private zones happen shortly after peering updates, but we observed the traffic reaching IPs directly (no DNS involvement). However, we saw a separate, lower-severity issue where cached DNS responses on older nodes allowed stale SRV entries for a peered subnet; tracked separately.
- Related failures: when autoscaler removed nodes quickly after a burst, some cleanup hooks were skipped leading to lingering NAT rules for up to 5 minutes in rare cases.
mitigation: Short-term mitigation (hotfix): add preflight check in node join flow to hold accepting tenant traffic until node-network-agent confirms VRF binding and iptables baseline applied. Implemented a 60s hold window and conservative deny-by-default rule that is replaced once reconciliation finishes. Deployed to prod dedicated pools 2026-03-11 04:30 UTC.
Customer communications: Notified impacted customers with mitigation details and isolated their workloads to avoid further exposure while fix rolled out.
Circuit-breaker: Added a guard in autoscaler controller to limit concurrent node joins per pool to reduce race windows.
long_term_fix: 1) Refactor node-network-agent reconciliation to use atomic update transactions for iptables and VRF bindings so that chains are created with the final tenant ID only once labels are present.
2) Introduce idempotent naming (UUID-based) for temporary chains during scale operations to avoid collisions with stale names derived from previous mappings.
3) Add unit and integration tests that simulate high-frequency node churn with the full join/leave lifecycle validating there are no cross-tenant rules at any point.
4) Add e2e Chaos test in CI that runs autoscaler scale-up/scale-down patterns against Dedicated pools and asserts isolation via active traffic probes.
rollout_plan: - Week 1 (hotfix): roll out hold-window and autoscaler concurrency limiter to all Dedicated regions (done 2026-03-11). Monitor infra for regressions and customer reports.
- Week 2-3: land atomic reconciliation refactor behind feature flag; run canary on one low-traffic pool for 48h.
- Week 4: if stable, expand rollout to remaining Dedicated pools and remove feature flag after 1 week of clean telemetry.
- Post-release: run retrospective and update runbooks/incident playbooks with new detection queries.
next_steps: - Diego to open PR for atomic iptables/VRF apply (WIP: branch net/atomic-apply).
- QA to schedule dedicated chaos e2e with autoscaler scenarios (request: 4h slot in cycle 2026-W12).
- SRE to add Grafana alerts for 'iptables chain creation without VRF binding' pattern and increase retention for packet captures for affected pools to 72h.
- PM to draft postmortem and customer-facing summary once long-term fix is merged.
